You are doing a focused code-review pass (Angle F: efficiency) on a git diff in the repo at /Users/jessitron/code/jessitron/mtg-deck-shuffler/.claude/worktrees/library-portal-ticket-12 (a git worktree). The full unified diff is saved at /tmp/review-diff.txt (also obtainable via `git -C <repo> diff main...HEAD`). It implements a "library portal" feature: dragging MTG card shapes onto their library "swallows" them, sending a card.returned.v1 event to a Spine service via a new Tabletop server route.

Read these new/changed files in full from the repo:
- apps/tabletop/src/client/shapes/cardSwallow.ts (new)
- apps/tabletop/src/client/shapes/LibraryPortalOverlay.tsx (new — renders on every animation frame via useValue during a drag)
- apps/tabletop/src/client/shapes/MtgCardShapeUtil.tsx (onTranslateEnd, getInterpolatedProps)
- apps/tabletop/src/client/shapes/zoneHitTest.ts (armedZoneIdSignal, topmostZoneAt)
- apps/tabletop/src/server/cardReturned.ts (new route handler)
- apps/tabletop/src/server/sendCardReturned.ts

YOUR TASK: Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O, independent operations run sequentially that could run in parallel, blocking work added to a hot path (a drag gesture, or the swallow's per-frame overlay rendering), or unnecessary re-renders. Also flag any long-lived closures capturing large scope (memory-leak risk). Specifically consider:
- `MtgCardShapeUtil.onTranslateEnd` now calls `topmostZoneAt(this.editor, this.editor.inputs.currentPagePoint)` in addition to whatever `handleTranslateEnd` internally does (which per cardZoneEntry.ts's `zoneAt()` ALSO calls `topmostZoneAt` on the shape's center) — is `topmostZoneAt` being computed twice redundantly on a normal (non-library) drop?
- `LibraryPortalOverlay.tsx`'s `useValue` callback calls `editor.getShapePageBounds`, `editor.pageToViewport`, and `editor.getZoomLevel()` — does `useArmedLibraryZoneId` (called separately, one level up) ALSO recompute `armedZoneIdSignal` redundantly alongside this?
- In `cardSwallow.ts`'s `completeSwallow`, `Promise.all([postCardReturned(send), sleep(SWALLOW_DURATION_MS)])` — is running the POST and the sleep in parallel actually correct/intentional (vs sequential), or does it risk the POST completing and then still waiting needlessly, or vice versa hiding a slow POST behind the animation only up to 500ms?
- Any place doing synchronous work inside a tldraw reactive `useValue`/signal computation that's more expensive than needed for something recomputed on every pointer-move during a drag.

Name the cheaper alternative for each finding.

Report up to 6 candidate findings as a JSON array with fields: file, line, summary, failure_scenario (state the concrete cost: wasted CPU/IO, dropped frames, memory retained). Keep your final response SHORT — just the JSON array. Do not fix anything, only report.

<system-reminder>
Other agents active in this session, addressable via SendMessage({to: name, message}): main, code-review.
</system-reminder>

content.text:
Confirmed: `onTranslateEnd` now always calls `topmostZoneAt` once itself (using `currentPagePoint`), and then for every non-library drop falls through to `handleTranslateEnd` → `zoneAt` → `topmostZoneAt` again (using the shape's bounds center) — a full re-scan of all page shapes, computed twice per drop on the common path.

Also confirmed `useArmedLibraryZoneId` and `LibraryPortalOverlay`'s own `useValue` both call `armedZoneIdSignal(editor).get()` — but that's a memoized `computed()` signal, so the second `.get()` is cheap (cached, not recomputed) — not a real finding, unlike the `topmostZoneAt` case which is a plain function called twice with no memoization.
